hero.title: Project Exodus
hero.subtitle: Live longer. Age healthier.
hero.intro: We're building the infrastructure for preventive health and longevity: All health data in one place, clearly presented, with AI support and medical quality assurance. Our goal: Help every person stay healthy longer and make the best decisions for a long, vital life.
hero.demoDesc: All your health data at a glance: lab results, medical letters, wearable data — structured as a timeline, clearly presented, always under your control.

vision.title: Why Exodus?
vision.titleSub: One platform instead of ten apps.
vision.desc: Today you need one app for lab results, one for fitness, one for supplements, one for the doctor. Exodus brings it all together — holistic, understandable, and secure.

cards.title: Health Vault / Data Wall
cards.desc: Lab results, medical letters, training and wearable data — all imported, structured, and visualized as a timeline.

cards.title: Simple as Instagram

cards.title: Supplement Ecosystem
cards.desc: Proprietary supplement line with custom formulations, partnerships (e.g. Biogena), and in-app purchasing — personalized to your profile.

cards.title: AI-powered Analytics
cards.desc: Step by step: from general explanations to personalized training and health plans.

cards.title: Core USP
cards.desc: Holistic coverage: Lab + Fitness + Supplements + medical care — instead of isolated solutions.

vision.diffDesc: Unlike tandemhealth.ai, Oura, Apple Health, Whoop, or specialized single-purpose apps, Exodus offers an integrated end-to-end platform: from data collection to AI analysis to medical approval.

features.glossDef: The ability to digitize unstructured medical documents (PDFs, scans) using AI, extract biomarkers, and visualize longitudinal trends over years.
Seamless aggregation of real-time biometrics (HRV, VO₂ Max, sleep stages) from various hardware providers into a central dashboard.
Use of explainable AI that reveals causal relationships between lifestyle and lab values, rather than just delivering isolated data points.
A process where generated health plans or lab analyses are reviewed and approved by licensed physicians.
A marketplace integrated directly into the app for personalized supplements or clinical medications based on individual data.
Providing sports science-based programs that dynamically incorporate stress and recovery data (RHR, HRV) into workout planning.
An architecture where sensitive health data is primarily stored and processed encrypted on the user's device.
The technological freedom to switch between different AI models (e.g. local LLMs for maximum privacy vs. powerful cloud models).
Demonstrable compliance with European data protection standards, including server locations in the EU and no unauthorized third-party sharing.

aiChoice.title: Bring your own AI
aiChoice.desc: Exodus is not a closed black box. The Health Vault is an open interface — you decide which AI model analyzes your health data: locally on your Mac, directly on your smartphone, or cloud-based when you explicitly opt in. This is crucial for data privacy and technically unique.

categories.title: Cloud Models (opt-in)
categories.claim: Full control — you decide when and what is shared

privacyPoints.title: GDPR compliant
privacyPoints.desc: Data only goes to the AI you choose — never automatically to the cloud.

privacyPoints.title: You decide
privacyPoints.desc: Switch models anytime. Access per analysis explicitly controllable.

privacyPoints.title: Local first
privacyPoints.desc: Default is always local. Cloud is explicit opt-in — no hidden sharing.

aiChoice.techDesc: The Health Vault implements an open API interface (MCP-compatible) — any compatible AI model can be integrated as an analysis engine. Data only leaves the Vault with explicit permission; local models get direct on-device access without network communication.

problem.title: Today: Data everywhere.
problem.titleSub: Tomorrow: a timeline that makes sense.
problem.desc: Health data is often scattered: PDFs, medical letters, lab values, wearable apps. This leads to a lack of overview, trends get lost, and decisions become difficult. Project Exodus brings this information into a structured timeline ("Health Data Wall").

how.title: Import → Understand → Approve
how.desc: In three simple steps: data in, understand, and if needed get medical approval.

steps.title: Import
steps.desc: Documents (PDF/scan) and wearable data are imported into the Vault and organized.

steps.title: Understand
steps.desc: The app translates values into clear explanations: What is it? Why relevant? What could I observe?

steps.title: Approve
steps.desc: When personalized plans are created, a doctor/therapist reviews and approves them.

how.safetyDesc: AI may suggest — but never decide unchecked. No diagnosis, no "therapy command".
how.figCaption: Three-step data flow: Import → Understand → Approve
how.exampleDesc: Instead of cryptic lab values, you get understandable cards that explain: What was measured? What does the value mean? What could I observe?

explainCards.title: Vitamin D — 28 ng/ml
explainCards.explanation: Vitamin D supports bones, immune system, and mood. Your value is in the lower range.
explainCards.observation: Watch for: fatigue, susceptibility to infections in winter. A trend across multiple measurements is more meaningful than a single value.

explainCards.title: TSH — 2.4 mU/L
explainCards.explanation: TSH controls the thyroid. Your value is in the normal range (0.4–4.0 mU/L).
explainCards.observation: No action needed. If symptoms like weight changes or cold sensitivity occur: consult your doctor.

how.importantNote: Important: Explanation cards provide general information — not individual diagnoses. They help you better understand your values and discuss them with your doctor.
how.phase2Desc: In Phase 2, the information system becomes a support system: The app can create personalized drafts based on scientific evidence (studies, guidelines) — for example nutritional adjustments or monitoring suggestions.
how.phase2Note: Phase 2 requires MDR conformity and clinical validation. Until then: general information only.

product.title: Three Product Paths — a Staged Model
product.desc: We start pragmatically (wellness app) and gradually build out clinical features. Each path has a clear regulatory boundary.

paths.title: Health Data Wall
paths.desc: Import, structure, display documents. Wellness-first, no MDR required.

paths.title: Evidence-to-Plan
paths.desc: Literature RAG + Clinician-in-the-Loop. Doctor can approve, modify, or reject AI drafts. "Why this?" explanation cards with safety logic.

paths.title: Sovereign Health AI Stack
paths.desc: EU/on-prem LLM, de-identification, policy engine, audit logs. Full digital sovereignty.

phases.title: Consumer App (Wellness/Vault)
phases.desc: Quick start, no MDR. Export, communication, "contact doctor". Supplements as parallel revenue stream.

phases.title: HCP Module (Physios/Doctors)
phases.desc: AI plan suggestions only with medical approval. Clinical evidence as foundation.

phases.title: Fully Certified MDR Product
phases.desc: Potentially reimbursable. Complete clinical validation and CE marking.

agent.title: Agentic Layer
agent.desc1: OpenClaw is a viral open-source AI agent by Austrian developer Peter Steinberger — 100,000+ GitHub stars in just weeks, one of the fastest-growing open-source projects ever. It runs locally on your own device and can be controlled via WhatsApp, Telegram, or iMessage.
agent.desc2: Exodus will be published as an official OpenClaw Skill Pack via ClawHub — with health-related capabilities for the agent, without OpenClaw ever seeing raw data from the Vault. Which AI model is used remains freely choosable — locally on the device or cloud-based via opt-in (

flowSteps.label: Exodus Vault
flowSteps.sub: Health data, lab values, and supplement history stored locally encrypted — no cloud required

flowSteps.label: Exodus Skill Pack (MCP Server)
flowSteps.sub: Exodus provides the agent with type-safe functions — OpenClaw only receives explicitly authorized data, never raw data or direct database access

flowSteps.label: OpenClaw Agent (local on user's device)
flowSteps.sub: Runs on your own device or server — receives commands via WhatsApp, Telegram, or iMessage and executes them autonomously

flowSteps.label: Supplement Shop (e.g. Biogena)
flowSteps.sub: Browser automation: Agent opens the shop, adds recommended products to cart — order only triggered after user confirmation

flowSteps.label: Confirmation & Vault Log
flowSteps.sub: Order confirmation and invoice are automatically saved in the Vault — complete history, accessible anytime

skills.desc: Delivers current AI-generated supplement recommendations from the Vault — tailored to the personal health profile
Gives the agent only explicitly authorized health data (e.g. specific biomarkers, lab values) — no full access
Compares available supplements based on shared lab values — returns specific recommendation with reasoning
Checks available and already ordered supplements in user profile — prevents duplicate orders
Triggers browser automation — opens configured shop and prepares order. Only finalized after user confirmation
Writes confirmation, invoice, and agent action log securely back to the Vault

securityItems: OpenClaw runs locally on the user's device — personal data never leaves the device. Exodus Vault only delivers explicitly authorized data via MCP; no direct database access.
Every agent action is logged in the Vault and can be viewed, canceled, or reversed by the user — complete transparency.
Orders are prepared but only triggered after explicit user confirmation (opt-in). No autonomous ordering without approval.
agent.techBasis: Exodus implements an MCP Server (Model Context Protocol) — the standardized interface between AI agents and external tools. The Skill Pack is published via ClawHub (the official OpenClaw skill directory with 5,400+ skills) and can be installed in minutes via clawhub install exodus. The agent authenticates with a user-specific token — no direct database access, no raw data, only explicitly defined function calls.

extFeatures: You see which data is shared
tech.intDesc: The Health Vault connects with wearables, HIS/ERP systems, clinical standards, research partners, scientific databases, and open protocols.
tech.openDataDesc: Public datasets as demand and impact evidence: chronic diseases, musculoskeletal complaints, diabetes trends, presenteeism.

security.title: Privacy by architecture — not just by policy.
security.desc: Health data is highly sensitive. Our core principle: data stays with the user. Synchronization and sharing only happen when you actively allow it.

cards.title: Local by Default
cards.desc: Data is primarily stored locally (encrypted). The app remains usable offline.

cards.title: Any Cloud — Your Choice
cards.desc: Sync is optional. You choose which cloud you use — ours, your own, or none at all. Data is encrypted there too.

cards.title: Controlled Sharing
cards.desc: Data type, timeframe, purpose, duration. Shares are revocable and traceable.

security.syncNote: You decide where your data is stored. The key always stays with you.
security.figCaption: Data flow: Device Vault → any cloud (key stays local)
security.sharingDesc: When you want to share data — e.g. with your doctor or a research project — you control exactly what is shared. Every share is granular and revocable.
security.revokeNote: Revoke anytime: You can withdraw any share at any time. Shared data is marked as "no longer available" at the recipient.

regulation.title: Regulation: We deliberately start "below" the medical device threshold.
regulation.desc: In the EU, classification largely depends on the "intended purpose." That's why we separate functions modularly and start with an information system: collect, structure, and display — plus general explanations.
regulation.disclaimer: This page is not legal advice. MDR/AI Act classification is being reviewed with experts in the project.
regulation.figCaption: Regulatory classification: Phase 1 (information system) vs. Phase 2 (MDR path)

roadmap.title: Roadmap: Now → Founding → Platform → Longevity Centers
roadmap.desc: Linz, April 2026. Prototype ready, FFG submitted, AWS Incubator applied. FFG small project submission on May 10. Company founding after first grant approval — then step-by-step build of a complete health ecosystem.
roadmap.fundingDesc: Purely grant-funded development — from low-threshold to substantial. Each stage builds on the previous one. Cumulative potential funding: over €400,000 (FFG + aws + tech2b + Upper Austria).
roadmap.fundingNote: Important for FFG submissions: most common rejection reason is 'too little development risk' — the technical risk must be clearly demonstrated. Mind the de minimis account: max. €300,000 in 3 tax years.

risks.title: Key Risks & Countermeasures
risks.desc: We name risks openly and have a clear countermeasure for each.

items.counter: Wellness-first start, modular intended purpose, MDR path only in Phase 2
LOIs, pilot project with clear boundaries, documented cooperation
Clinician-in-the-Loop, explainable AI (EU-compliant), safety layer, no automatic recommendations
Privacy-by-design, cryptographic storage, EU hosting, security audits
Staged plan: FFG Projekt.Start → Innovation voucher → Small project → aws First Incubator → Impact Innovation → Base program
Early classification, explainability requirements (Art. 13 EU AI Act) from the start, open-source models preferred

Spike API, ELGA-related structures, open standards

risks.footer: Additional risks: liability, ethics/adherence, GPU costs. Countermeasures: patent/IP plan, gamification, partner network.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.desc: The most important questions about data privacy, product, regulation, and funding — briefly answered.

items.a: By default locally in the Vault (on your device). Optionally sync can be activated — you choose which cloud you use (ours, your own, or others). In any case, data is stored encrypted.

items.q: Do I have to use your cloud?
items.a: No. You can use any cloud or work entirely without sync. The key always stays with you.

items.q: Does data automatically go to AI models?
items.a: No. Analyses are only possible after explicit approval, with clear limits: data type, timeframe, purpose, and duration.

items.q: Can operators view my health data?
items.a: Target: as little as possible. Operator access is not 'standard' but must be technically and organizationally strictly limited.

items.q: What happens if I lose my device?
items.a: Without sync, data loss is possible. With sync, recovery is possible. This trade-off is made transparent.
Personalized plans are not deployed unchecked. A medical professional reviews and approves them.
No, not in Phase 1. Focus: collect, structure, display, explain generally.
Yes. Portability and deletion are core principles (details will be specified in the product).

items.q: What distinguishes Exodus from Oura, Apple Health, or Whoop?
items.a: Individual apps each cover only one area (fitness, sleep, lab). Exodus is an integrated end-to-end platform: Lab + Fitness + Supplements + medical care in one app.

items.q: Does the app need a medical device certificate (CE)?
items.a: Phase 1 (Health Data Wall) is an information system — no MDR needed. Only when personalized therapy/health plans are created by AI (Phase 2) do we need CE marking under MDR IIa.
Supplements are a parallel revenue stream: own products and partnerships (e.g. Biogena). Purchase directly in the app.
Purely grant-funded development via a funding cascade from FFG, aws, tech2b, and Upper Austrian funds. Cumulative potential: over €400,000.
